solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Top puller reveals bad loser's vainglorious erection

blocks.note: to trump is to top or beat, as with a card of the winning suit
one who tows something is a puller

explanation.surface: A smutty sneer at a sore loser whose showy building is likened to something rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Top' as a verb and 'puller' as a noun built from 'tow'; the bad loser is Donald Trump, who refused to accept defeat in 2020.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York skyscraper bearing his name is the boastful building put up by the politician who would not concede.

clue.text: Hard to escape HRH's penile dysfunction – return to full capacity?

indicators.note: whatever escapes gets away, so that letter leaves the group
something that does not function properly is out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken letter by letter, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A tabloid jibe about a royal's bedroom trouble, wondering whether he will ever perform again.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one H from HRH'S PENILE and rearrange the remaining nine letters; the possessive S counts as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill something up again, bringing stocks back to their earlier level.

clue.text: Brief version of Private Eye by American wise guy?

blocks.note: Private Eye is a magazine, and MAG is that word shortened
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: Asks whether an American smart alec has produced a condensed edition of the satirical magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye, the British satirical fortnightly where this puzzle appears, is a magazine; 'wise guy' sounds like slang for a smart alec but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a learned sage or magician, like the three Magi who followed the star, so literally a man of wisdom.

clue.text: Was a consumer about to be overwhelmed by 'mangled nuts' disease?

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
being overwhelmed is being engulfed, so one part ends up enclosed by the other
a mangled thing is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a consumer eats, so 'was a consumer' is the past tense
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gruesome question about an eater catching some ailment linked to crushed testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was a consumer' is just past-tense eating; the turned-round eating word lands between the first and second letters of the jumbled four.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms and lockjaw, so it is a specific example of an illness.

clue.text: Words of question-avoiding politician that he might have to eat?

definitions.text: that he might have to eat

blocks.note: first meaning: vague, evasive talk that fills time without answering

blocks.clueFragment: that he might have to eat
blocks.note: second meaning: a crisp batter cake with a grid pattern

explanation.surface: A dig at a slippery politician who may one day have to eat his own words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat' plays on the idiom of eating your words: here the words themselves are a breakfast food.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both rambling evasive speech and the griddled batter cake served with syrup.

clue.text: Degenerate Dicky's share?

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute, degenerate man about town
dicky is British slang for unwell or unreliable, as is off

explanation.surface: Sounds like asking about the cut taken by some debauched character called Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a man's name but is the British adjective meaning shaky or poorly (a dicky heart), and 'Degenerate' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a commission or cut of the proceeds, often an illicit one, taken by an intermediary.

clue.text: see 28ac.
Start to squeeze nuts hard – terrible institution leading to a soldier's passing out

definitions.text: institution leading to a soldier's passing out

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: first letter of the word
taken as written, eight letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: A painful scene of crushed genitals ending in a soldier fainting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing out' suggests fainting after the squeeze, but it is the parade where officer cadets graduate; 'nuts' looks like the anagram signal yet is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Military Academy in Berkshire trains British Army officers, who finish their course at a passing-out parade.

clue.text: Be condescending, ending badly with name struck off

indicators.note: done badly means done wrong, so the letters come out in a wrong order
being struck off a list means being removed from it

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Sounds like a haughty professional whose career ends in disgrace when struck off the register.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDING has two Ns; lose one and rearrange what remains. 'Struck off' evokes a doctor or lawyer barred from practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something one considers beneath oneself, a grudging, superior act.

clue.text: Plug from piss artist drinking stuff

indicators.note: whoever is drinking takes something inside, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: piss artist is British slang for a heavy drinker, a sot
to stuff yourself is to pig, eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone getting a plug, perhaps a recommendation, from a drunk with a glass in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' could be a free advert, but here it is the stopper; 'stuff' is a verb meaning gorge, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small peg or tap used to stop up the vent hole of a cask, so a stopper.

clue.text: Not coming clean with your lover?

definitions.text: Not coming clean with your lover?

blocks.clueFragment: Not coming clean with your lover?
blocks.note: surface reading: hiding the truth from a partner, perhaps about an affair
setter's reading: not actually reaching orgasm, and pretending otherwise in bed

explanation.surface: Someone being less than honest with a partner about what they have been up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming clean' means confessing, but split it and 'coming' is sexual climax: the partner pretends to have one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for simulating pleasure or ability you lack, classically a feigned orgasm.

clue.text: Er, my boy, being squeezed by mate is intimate

indicators.note: what is squeezed by something is held tight inside it

blocks.note: a mate is a friend, a pal
taken as written
a parent's boy is their son

explanation.surface: A hesitant parent describing a son caught up in a close friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Er' is not hesitation but two letters of fodder; it and the boy go together inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal matters are private ones concerning a person's own life, close to intimate in the sense of private.

clue.text: Where a tosser came to be easily accessible?

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a tosser is a masturbator, who finishes on his own palm
second meaning: available, close by and ready for use

explanation.surface: Seems to ask where some idiot turned up to make himself available.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosser is British slang for a contemptible person, literally a masturbator; 'came' is taken in its sexual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept nearby and ready for use is the idiom for available whenever needed.

clue.text: Suffocating? Don't broadcast so much

blocks.note: first meaning: stuffy, without fresh oxygen
second meaning, split in two: put out fewer transmissions

explanation.surface: A complaint about stifling media saturation, telling the channels to cut back on output.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to read the second half as an instruction: to air a programme is to broadcast it.
explanation.definitionFit: An airless room lacks ventilation, so it feels stifling and makes breathing hard.

clue.text: Speaker's indiscretion? Filling peer with false tales

indicators.note: a false version is not the true arrangement, so the letters are reordered
filling something means going inside it

blocks.note: to peer is to look closely
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker gossiping, stuffing a member of the Lords with lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' and 'peer' suggest Parliament, but peer is a verb and the speaker is anyone talking; read the clue as filling peer with the jumbled tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless chatter that gives away secrets, as in the wartime slogan, is an indiscretion committed by someone talking.

clue.text: Carrie partying with Fay? That is out – quite a different matter

indicators.note: people partying are moving about wildly, so the letters are scrambled
something out is gone, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Gossip that Carrie Johnson partied with someone named Fay, then the matter is said to be another story.
explanation.walkthrough: Carrie Johnson, the Prime Minister's wife, was linked to the lockdown parties; strip the two letters of 'that is' from the pair of names and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To say one thing is a long way from another is the idiom for being very different from it.

clue.text: Inject new life into Starmer's ultimate barmy rest-cure

indicators.note: the ultimate thing is the very last, so only the final letter is used
barmy is British slang for crazy, so the letters go haywire

blocks.note: final letter of the surname
taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: Suggests the Labour leader's crazy final plan of a long rest to revive his party.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer led the Labour Party; his last letter joins the eight of 'rest-cure' and all nine are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurrect is to bring back from death or revive something dormant, giving it fresh vitality.

clue.text: Mad hot party, leader not present – showing Covid symptom?

indicators.note: something mad is deranged, so the letters lose their order
the leader of a word is its first letter, and it is absent

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its opening letter removed

explanation.surface: A wild Downing Street lockdown party where the Prime Minister claimed not to be there, with guests coughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader not present' sounds like Boris Johnson's excuses over Partygate, but it simply removes a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A throaty voice is hoarse and rasping, as with the sore throat typical of a Covid infection.

clue.text: Bump off granny? It would go to your head

definitions.text: It would go to your head

blocks.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
a granny is a type of knot, an insecure reef knot

explanation.surface: A dark question about murdering an elderly relative and the guilt or gain going to your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granny' is not a grandmother but the granny knot, a badly tied reef knot; 'go to your head' sounds figurative but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is hair tied up in a bun or knot on the crown, so it sits literally on the scalp.

clue.text: Game Tory put on trial

blocks.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician, willing to play along, ends up in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like an adjective meaning willing, but it is the noun for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a competition between rivals, so a sporting match or game is an example.

clue.text: Eye's description of storming of Capitol

indicators.note: a storming crowd rushes in wildly, throwing things into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Private Eye's own account of the January 2021 riot at the US Capitol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' looks like the magazine's name, but it means the organ of sight here.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical is the adjective relating to sight and vision, so it describes things to do with eyes.

clue.text: Gorge – no matter what – in study

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or pore over
'any' means whichever, no matter what

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to binge whatever happens while in their study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' reads as a verb, overeat, but it is the noun for a ravine; con meaning study is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep valley with steep rock walls, which is what a gorge is.

clue.text: Being inactive like Labour leader, piss about

indicators.note: the leader of a word is at its front, so its first letter is taken
turning about means facing the opposite way, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: 'like' and 'as' both introduce a comparison
first letter of the word
both are slang for urinate

explanation.surface: A jibe that a sluggish opposition leader just messes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss about' sounds like the idiom for wasting time, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is dormant and doing nothing, and the word also describes limbs or minds that are numb or idle.

clue.text: Seasonal deliveryman, somewhat unpleasant (Amazon)

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word break

explanation.surface: A sour remark on an Amazon courier making Christmas drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed company name seems a jokey aside, but its first letter completes the run begun in the preceding word.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas brings presents to children every December, a festive delivery round.

clue.text: Showing crafty skill, devious rat lives with loveless Tory

definitions.note: the clue's phrase describes the quality in use; the answer is the noun for that skill

indicators.note: something devious takes a winding route, so the letters stray from their order
love is zero, the letter O in crosswords, and 'less' takes it away

blocks.note: taken as written
to live is to be, so 'lives' gives 'is'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scheming political rat cohabiting with a cold-hearted Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O from the zero score in tennis; a 'loveless' Tory has that letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative ability or craftsmanship, the talent displayed by someone working skilfully.

clue.text: It could be a No.10 bonk

blocks.note: first meaning: a threaded fastener, sold in numbered gauges such as a number ten
second meaning: British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: Hints at a sex scandal at No. 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: No.10 points to Downing Street, but it is a standard gauge of the threaded fastener; bonk is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the threaded metal fastener sized by gauge number and, in slang, the sexual act.

clue.text: Large body associated with a lying bum – awkward

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters come out wrong

blocks.note: the United Nations is a large international body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large organisation embarrassingly tied to a dishonest layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like a noun for a tramp or backside but works as the slang adjective for bad; 'large body' means an organisation, not a fat person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainly means clumsy and lacking grace in movement, which matches awkward in its physical sense.

clue.text: Prudence has Brenda calling

blocks.note: prudence is care or caution
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: One woman phoning another, Prudence ringing Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Both names look like people, but Prudence is a common noun and Brenda is the magazine's long-running name for the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation or profession, the line of work someone pursues through life.

clue.text: (& 7ac.) Evil aspect of Democrat party, confining biblical craft

indicators.note: to confine is to shut in, so one part is enclosed by another

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
a party is one of the opposing teams or factions in a dispute or contest
Noah's ark is the vessel from Genesis

explanation.surface: Paints the Democratic Party as sinister, harbouring religious zealots.
explanation.walkthrough: Join the abbreviation and the party first, then slip the boat in just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, popularised by Star Wars, means the sinister or wicked part of someone's nature.

clue.text: To get involved in a fight – that's Putin's focus and view supporting

definitions.text: To get involved in a fight

indicators.note: the focus is the central point, so the middle letter is taken

blocks.note: middle letter of the five-letter surname
an angle is a point of view
to be with someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Describes Putin's single-minded war aims and those backing him in the Ukraine conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the possessive S when finding the centre: the middle of the five-letter name is its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tangle with someone is to become embroiled in an argument or physical scuffle with them.
